summary.title: Simple Anomaly Detection Using Plain SQL
summary.one_liner: You learn how to detect anomalies in time-series data such as server logs using only PostgreSQL SQL: mean, standard deviation, z-scores, sliding windows, and thresholds, with no extra dependencies.
keywords: fill gaps in time series sql
takeaways: Define a reasonable value with the mean and a deviation with the standard deviation, then flag values outside a z-score threshold as anomalies.
Use generate_series and a VALUES list to build a complete time axis so zero-count periods are not missing from the data.
Compute a rolling mean and standard deviation per status code with a PostgreSQL window function over the previous 60 rows.
Backtest different z-score thresholds on past data, and add a minimum entries threshold to avoid alerts on single events.
Suppress repeated alerts so that one anomaly triggers only one notification rather than one per minute.
summary.summary: The article builds a simple anomaly detector using only SQL in PostgreSQL, without external tools or statistical libraries. It starts with a small numeric series, computing the mean, standard deviation, and z-score to flag outliers, then applies the same approach to a server log summary table of HTTP status codes per minute. It shows how to fill gaps with a generated time axis, compute the last-value z-score for alerts, and run backtests with a sliding 60-row window to tune the threshold. It finishes by adding a minimum-entries threshold to reduce noise and discusses avoiding repeated alerts for the same ongoing anomaly.
